learning_outcomes.text: Effective use of information sources and resources of communication and assisted professional training (Internet portals, specialized software applications, databases, online courses, etc.) both in Romanian and in a language of international circulation.
Improving English knowledge to understand and produce accurate academic and scientific texts in English.
Understanding written or verbal texts on topics related to the field of engineering in general and the chosen specialization in particular.
Producing written texts or expressing oneself verbally in English.
Acquiring field-related vocabulary in English and the completion of documents that are specific to the chosen field of study.

syllabus_topics: Material types: Metals and non-metals. Elements, compounds and mixtures. Composite materials. Vocabulary and speaking exercises.
Polymers. Natural and synthetic polymers. Thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics. Reading. Vocabulary and conversation exercises. Revision of numerals.
Material properties (I). Tensile strength and deformation. Elasticity and plasticity. Stages in elastic and plastic deformation. Vocabulary exercises.
Material properties (I). Hardness. Fatigue, fracture toughness and creep. Basic thermal properties. Reading and vocabulary exercises.
Interconnection: vocabulary relating to attaching and supporting and fitting together different parts, specific to the engineering domain (revision exercises).
Mechanical fasteners (I). Bolts. Preload in bolted joints. Washers. Listening and speaking exercises. Revision: Countable and uncountable nouns.
Mechanical fasteners (2). Screws. Screw anchors and rivets. Vocabulary and speaking exercises.
Non-mechanical joints: welding, brazing, soldering, adhesives. Reading and vocabulary exercises.
Referring to types of force and deformation. The concept of failure in engineering. Vocabulary and speaking exercises.
Expressing numbers and calculations. Decimals and fractions. Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. (Listening and vocabulary exercises).
Referring to the electrical supply. Direct current and alternating current. AC generation and supply. DC generation and use. (Reading and exercises).
Referring to circuits and components. Simple circuits. Mains AC circuits and switchboards. Printed and integrated circuits. Electrical and electronic components. (Reading and conversation exercises).
Referring to engines and motors. Types and functions of engines and motors. Reading and vocabulary exercises.
Referring to energy and temperature. Forms of energy. Energy efficiency. Work and power.
teaching_methods: Presentation of the course with video projector, on the board or online
assessment_rules: Students are required to solve exercises meant at testing the knowledge acquired during the semester. A minimum mark of 5 requires knowledge of fundamental notions without details. For a mark of 10, thorough knowledge of all subjects is required.
